zh.title: 美國航空於美國機場首度引進合成永續航空燃料並完成客運航班
zh.summary: 美國航空於科波斯克里斯蒂啟用合成燃油；執飛前往達拉斯客機；符合Jet A規範
body: 美國航空（American Airlines）於客運航班上使用電轉液體合成永續航空燃料（eSAF），該航班由旗下班機以巴西航空工業（Embraer）E175機型執飛，從科波斯克里斯蒂國際機場（CRP）飛往達拉斯/愛德華之沃斯國際機場（DFW）。美國航空與燃料製造商Infinium表示，這是首次有非生物基質原料製成的永續航空燃料供應至美國商業機場。
這批電轉液體燃料由Infinium位於德克薩斯州科波斯克里斯蒂的Pathfinder設施生產，並在注入科波斯克里斯蒂國際機場（CRP）的共用油槽前與傳統航空燃油進行混合。該燃料經過嚴格測試，符合Jet A燃油的ASTM國際標準規範，因此可直接用於現有機型發動機與機場加油設備系統，無需進行任何技術修改。
Infinium採用廢棄二氧化碳與再生電力生產此類合成燃料，而非使用餐飲廢油或植物原料等生物基質。根據該公司說明，其生產的電轉液體永續航空燃料與傳統石油基航空燃油相比，在其全生命週期中可減少90%以上的溫室氣體排放量。
此外，美國航空已與Infinium簽署商業採購協議，將購入目前正在建設中的Project Roadrunner工廠所生產的商業規模電轉液體燃料。該設施預計於2027年開始生產與交付，未來每年預計生產超過500萬加侖的電轉液體永續燃料，推動綠色技術從早期投資進入商業實踐。

en.title: American Airlines Operates Commercial Flight Using Synthetic SAF Delivered to US Airport
en.summary: American Airlines operated a flight from Corpus Christi to Dallas Fort Worth using synthetic sustainable fuel.
body: American Airlines has completed a commercial passenger flight using electro sustainable aviation fuel (eSAF) supplied directly to a commercial airport in the United States. The flight was operated using an Embraer E175 regional jet flying from Corpus Christi International Airport (CRP) to Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW). American Airlines and fuel developer Infinium stated that the operation marked the first time sustainable aviation fuel produced without biobased feedstocks was delivered to a US commercial airport.

The eSAF was produced by Infinium at its Pathfinder facility in Corpus Christi, Texas. Prior to being delivered into common fuel storage tanks at Corpus Christi International Airport (CRP), the synthetic fuel was blended with conventional petroleum jet fuel. The fuel was thoroughly tested to ensure it met ASTM specifications for Jet A, enabling it to be utilized in existing commercial aircraft engines and airport fueling systems without requiring specialized modifications.

Infinium manufactures the synthetic fuel utilizing captured waste carbon dioxide and renewable electricity rather than relying on biological feedstocks such as waste cooking oil or agricultural plant material. According to Infinium, its eSAF process can reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions by more than 90% compared to conventional petroleum-based jet fuel during regular airline operations.

In addition to the initial passenger flight, American Airlines has signed an agreement to purchase commercial volumes of eSAF from Infinium's Project Roadrunner plant, which is currently under construction. The manufacturing facility is expected to begin production and deliveries in 2027, with plans to eventually produce more than 5 million gallons of synthetic fuel annually for commercial aviation use.
